clue.text: Flyer produced by artist during spell in jail

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
in the sense 'in the course of'
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang 'bird-lime' for time

explanation.surface: A leaflet turned out by a painter while serving a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet, but it is a bird. Doing bird is British slang for serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbird is any bird whose call is thought to foretell rain, such as the green woodpecker, so it is a creature that flies.

clue.text: Knight stopping revision of a mutual description of the Fall?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the knight goes inside
a revision reworks the letters of a mutual

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight interrupting an edit of a shared account of humanity's Fall from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fall suggests Adam and Eve, but it is the American word for the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumnal describes things belonging to autumn, which Americans call fall.

clue.text: Crazy, awful place — Brazil may be in it

parts.note: nuts means mad
hell is any dreadful place

explanation.surface: A mad, dreadful place to live, which the country Brazil might be.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil looks like the country, but it is the Brazil nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil nut grows inside a hard casing, so its shell is where the kernel sits.

clue.text: Teaching alphabet including old Greek character

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the alphabet contains the letter for old

parts.note: ITA is the Initial Teaching Alphabet, a phonetic alphabet once used to teach reading

explanation.surface: A school alphabet that includes an archaic Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a written symbol of Greek.

clue.text: Exchange views on princess's malediction

parts.note: Di, as in Princess Diana, with the possessive s
a cuss is a curse

explanation.surface: Talking over the curse put on a princess, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss a topic is to talk it over, trading opinions about it.

clue.text: Attract newlywed to cross key part of castle, perhaps

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it

indicators.note: the bride's letters go across the key, enclosing it

parts.note: a bride has just married
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Tempting a new bride to come over to a crucial bit of the castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is a liftable bridge over a moat, a typical feature of castle defences; the perhaps marks it as an example.

clue.text: Fish endlessly on island, a Mediterranean one

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the fish

parts.note: a sardine is a small fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sardines in endless supply on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is a large Italian island in the Mediterranean, the 'one' standing for island.

clue.text: Canvas giving trouble after ship crosses river

indicators.note: the word for trouble comes after the rest
the ship's letters go across the river, one on each side

parts.note: SS is steamship
the Tay is a Scottish river
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sail causes problems once the vessel crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a sail rigged on a stay; sails are made of canvas, so canvas stands for a sail.

clue.text: Irish girl meeting conservationists, a thorn in the flesh

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: An Irish woman joins the heritage lobby and becomes a constant nuisance to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in the flesh is an idiom for a persistent source of annoyance, which is exactly what an irritant is.

clue.text: Group of workers covered by nation's laws

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits inside it, so the workers' group goes within

parts.note: a nation is a state, so nation's is read as STATE'S
TU is a trade union

explanation.surface: A trade union finds itself bound by the legislation of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in nation's is ignored, giving a word that also reads as the plural of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written laws passed by a legislature, so the two words are plural synonyms.

clue.text: Spineless fish extremely lazy about fighting

indicators.note: the fish goes around the fighting, as one word wrapped about another

parts.note: cod is a common food fish
war is fighting on a large scale

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of lazy

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A fish too idle to bother taking part in a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Spineless is a figurative word for lacking courage, so it is a synonym for being fainthearted.

clue.text: Bury model, one who intrudes

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
one who poses for an artist is a poser

explanation.surface: An instruction to bury a fashion model, then a description of a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury, with its capital, could suggest the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An interposer is someone who puts themselves between others, an intruder or interferer.

clue.text: S American instrument mostly without a label on

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the instrument goes around the rest
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: the piano is a musical instrument
taken as written
a tag is a label
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South American instrument is played nearly bare, with no label attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Patagonian comes from Patagonia, at the southern tip of Argentina and Chile.

clue.text: Woman's articles incorporating news

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body, so the articles contain the other letter

parts.note: AN and A are the two forms of the indefinite article
N stands for new, read here from news

explanation.surface: Magazine pieces belonging to a woman that include current events.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Howl worried upper-class Liberal repeatedly at first

indicators.note: the pair of letters is given again
the repeated letters come before the rest

parts.note: U means upper-class and L is the abbreviation for Liberal
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: An anxious posh Liberal wails over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: UL twice, then ATE: 'ate' is the past of eat in the sense of fret or gnaw at.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to wail or howl, a long high trembling cry.

clue.text: A French press chief accepts reverse, lacking support

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the other letters surround the reverse

parts.note: un is French for a
an editor, ED, heads a newspaper
to back a car is to reverse it

explanation.surface: A French newspaper boss takes a step back, having lost his backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbacked means without backers, not supported by anyone.

clue.text: Doddery duke missing from Beds town

indicators.note: missing from means the letter for duke is taken out

parts.note: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, abbreviated Beds

explanation.surface: A doddering duke has gone absent from a Bedfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Beds looks like furniture, but is the abbreviation of Bedfordshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone doddery is shaky on their feet, so they are physically unsteady.

clue.text: Weirdo backing party finally organised dance

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of organised

parts.note: only its final letter is used
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An eccentric supporting the party who in the end arranged the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is an eccentric or strange person, the same sense as weirdo.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase some African lilies primarily for celebration

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so purchase some is taken by sound

parts.note: buy any, said quickly

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of African and lilies

parts.note: only the opening letters of these two words are used

explanation.surface: Buying some African lilies, said to be mainly for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The def is the noun: a biennial can be a festival held every two years.
explanation.definitionFit: A biennial is an event held every two years, such as an arts festival, a kind of recurring festivity.

clue.text: Doctor regales son, showing generosity

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of regales are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged with the son

explanation.surface: A physician entertains a boy, showing great kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a noun but is a verb meaning to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts, so it is a synonym for liberality.

clue.text: American writer, female, Emily Dickinson, for example?

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American poet and storyteller
Tess is a woman's name, as in Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A woman writer from America, the reclusive poet Emily Dickinson.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the term is old-fashioned for a female poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson was an American woman who wrote verse, so she is an example of a female poet.

clue.text: Vehicle husband used in wild, uncultivated country

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A coach with a married man aboard is driven out into wild terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is wild uncleared land, especially in Australia or Africa, far from towns or farms.

clue.text: Fruit web-footed bird found by touring English rivers

parts.note: a goose has webbed feet

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the word goes around the letters for English and rivers

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river, so two rivers give two Rs

explanation.surface: A goose is seen beside some fruit while travelling around English waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the abbreviation for river, so rivers gives two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The gooseberry is a tart green berry grown on a thorny bush, so it is a fruit.

clue.text: Instrument in Cambridge college keeping in time

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the college surrounds the next word

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument at a Cambridge college keeps the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument, so it is one kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Lively spirit one observed in little sibling

indicators.note: the numeral is seen inside the sibling word

parts.note: bro is the short form of brother

explanation.surface: A spark of vitality spotted in a baby brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or vivacity, a lively energy in performance or manner.

clue.text: Most ancient member of upper chamber breaking ties

parts.note: an earl is a peer who could sit in the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber

indicators.note: breaking smashes the word ties into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The oldest peer in the Lords is breaking his family connections.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper house of the British Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means first in time, so it describes whatever is the oldest of a set.

clue.text: Revolutionary shelter informer provided for marine plant

indicators.note: revolutionary is read as turning round, so the word for shelter goes backwards

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A rebel gives a hiding place to a supergrass, who becomes a seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary looks like a rebel's adjective but signals turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eelgrass is a seagrass growing in shallow coastal water, so it is a plant of the sea.

clue.text: Joint ought to be livelier, ultimately

parts.note: should means ought to

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of each of the words be and livelier

parts.note: only the last letter of each word is used

explanation.surface: A cut of meat that, in the end, needs more pep.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint looks like a cut of roast, which a shoulder also is; here it is the body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder is the ball-and-socket articulation linking arm and torso, so it is a body joint.
